cases.question: My first flight was delayed by bad weather and I missed my connection. Both flights were on one Northstar ticket. Will you put me on another flight for free?

matches.body:
## 1. Protected connections
A missed connection and a refund are separate decisions. Use this policy for replacement travel and NS-REF-2026 for refunds. Hotel assistance is assessed separately under NS-CARE-2026.

### 1.1 Covered transportation
A protected itinerary has at least two domestic Northstar-operated flights on the same ticket and reservation, sold as one continuous journey. The first flight must be disrupted before the onward flight's boarding cutoff. Separate tickets, codeshares, interline travel and international itineraries are outside this policy; refer those passengers to a specialist.

### 1.2 Confirming a missed connection
Compare actual inbound gate arrival, required transfer time and the onward boarding cutoff. A delayed inbound flight does not prove a missed connection if onward boarding remains open. Missing or contradictory operational times require review.

## 2. Rebooking and passenger choice
Rebooking eligibility, an available offer and a confirmed ticket are different stages. Staff must explain which stage has actually been reached.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. Seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed.

### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

### 2.3 Passenger decision
Record an offer as OFFERED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED or EXPIRED, including its timestamp and notification channel. Expiry or silence does not prove acceptance. A passenger may decline an alternative without losing an otherwise qualifying refund option.

### 2.4 Boarding feasibility
An aircraft still at the gate may already be closed for boarding. Use recorded boarding events and realistic transfer constraints, rather than scheduled departure alone. Escalate conflicting timestamps instead of guessing.

### 2.5 Offer versus confirmed booking
A text offering another flight does not mean the passenger is booked. Distinguish SEARCHED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, TICKETED and FLOWN. Confirmation requires an actual ticketed reservation. If no seats are available, record NO_CURRENT_INVENTORY: recovery eligibility remains, but transport is not confirmed.

### 2.6 Changed routing
A different airport, additional connection or substantial arrival change may affect refund eligibility. Check accessibility needs before presenting a routing as suitable. Fare price alone does not establish suitability.

### 2.7 Required information
Record the original ticket, affected segments, boarding and arrival times, available alternatives, passenger choice and applicable policy version. An unresolved cause does not prevent protected rebooking; cause matters separately for passenger care.

### 2.8 Conflicting messages
A gate agent, app and phone agent may show different inventory snapshots. Identify the current offer and whether a ticket exists. Multiple messages are not multiple confirmed bookings. Tell the passenger which offer replaced an earlier proposal.

## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization
Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher. Before booking independently, obtain written authorization stating the maximum reimbursable rate and approved dates. A receipt or verbal suggestion alone does not establish reimbursement approval.

### 4.7 Approved cause controls
The latest authorized, approved final investigation controls eligibility, even if a gate announcement initially said weather. A later unapproved draft cannot override an approved finding. Consult NS-CAUSE-2026 for investigation states.

### 4.8 Eligibility versus fulfillment
Full partner hotels do not remove eligibility. Record fulfillment separately as NOT_REQUESTED, SEARCHING, VOUCHER_AUTHORIZED, VOUCHER_ISSUED, RECEIPT_PENDING or CLOSED. Authorization is not proof of an issued voucher or booked room. Arrange alternative approved accommodation or escalate capacity problems.

### 4.9 Residence verification
Do not substitute billing address, nationality, telephone area code or trip origin for verified residence. Conflicting residence sources require authorized verification before deciding the home-metro condition.

A passenger who flies that replacement generally cannot obtain a full used-ticket refund under the change remedy. A missed connection alone remains insufficient to decide.

matches.body:
## 3. Qualifying disruption and passenger decision
The approved cause does not determine whether a cancellation or significant itinerary change qualifies. Weather-related changes can qualify just as airline-controlled changes can.

### 3.1 Cancellation
A canceled covered flight qualifies for assessment when the passenger declines substitute travel. Do not treat an ordinary delay as a cancellation. Verify the carrier's actual flight status.

### 3.2 Domestic significant-change threshold
A replacement scheduled to arrive at the final destination at least three hours later than originally scheduled meets the domestic arrival-change threshold. Departure at least three hours earlier can also qualify. Compare timezone-aware scheduled timestamps from the original ticket and replacement offer.

### 3.3 Passenger choice
Record whether the passenger requested a refund, declined replacement travel, accepted a credit or traveled. An unanswered offer does not prove acceptance or rejection. Verify delivery and expiry before deciding what response occurred.

### 3.4 Replacement flight already used
A passenger who flew the replacement generally cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under this disruption remedy. Arrival five hours late does not change that rule. Separate remedies for unused travel, downgrade or optional-service fees may still apply.

### 3.5 Final destination, not first-leg delay
A first flight arriving four hours late does not by itself establish the final-arrival change. A later connection may reduce the difference; a short inbound delay can also cause an overnight arrival change. Without replacement final-arrival information, the significant-change test remains unresolved.

### 3.6 Offer status
CREATED, DELIVERED, VIEWED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and FLOWN describe different events. DELIVERED means a notification reached the passenger's channel, not that they accepted travel. An internally generated voucher or offer does not close a refund request.

### 3.7 Partly used tickets
If the passenger flew the first segment but declines qualifying onward travel, assess the unused ticket portion using coupon accounting. Do not promise the entire fare or calculate a dollar amount without ticket-value records. Eligibility and refund amount are separate questions.

### 3.8 Other significant changes
A changed airport, additional connection or qualifying cabin downgrade may matter even when the arrival difference is under three hours. Compare the original and replacement itineraries before deciding. Duration is not the only qualifying criterion.

## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

### 3.1 Preliminary report
An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

### 3.2 Cause not yet confirmed
UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an open investigation means NEEDS_REVIEW for hotel or meal decisions that depend on controllability. Request the approved cause rather than promising payment or treating uncertainty as a weather exclusion. Rebooking eligibility is assessed separately.

### 3.3 Final finding
An authorized analyst must identify the controlling cause, document the reasoning and sign the final revision. A finalized, approved mechanical finding can supersede an earlier provisional weather remark. Verify that the finding concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight.

### 3.4 Mixed causes
When weather and an internal problem both contributed, identify which cause prevented timely operation during the relevant interval. Do not count keywords or assume any weather mention excludes assistance. Keep MIXED_PENDING when the evidence cannot resolve the controlling cause.

### 3.5 Causal sequence
Weather may delay an aircraft before a later crew problem prevents departure. A maintenance note may concern a different aircraft after a swap. Compare the chronology and affected segment; the last event mentioned is not necessarily the controlling cause.

### 3.6 Evidence precedence
The latest authorized, signed final investigation takes precedence over preliminary gate comments. Preserve the earlier observation, its timestamp and the approved revision explaining the change. Operational timestamps establish when events occurred; they do not by themselves establish why. Never overwrite an earlier record to hide a changed decision.

### 3.7 Timestamp conflicts
Compare timezone-aware or UTC timestamps from reconciled operational records. A later ingestion time is not proof that an event happened later. If material times conflict, seek review rather than selecting the most convenient value.

### 3.8 Investigation states
The lifecycle is REPORTED, INVESTIGATING, PROPOSED and FINAL_APPROVED. PROPOSED is a draft awaiting authorized approval; it cannot override a valid approved finding. REOPENED means new evidence requires review of the earlier result. Keep the status and cause code as separate fields.

answer.answer: Under the current policy (NS-CONN-2026, effective January 1, 2026), yes in principle: weather is not an exclusion for rebooking. A "protected" itinerary is two or more domestic Northstar-operated flights on the same ticket and reservation sold as one continuous journey, with the first flight disrupted before the onward flight's boarding cutoff. For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to your original destination at no additional fare — this covers weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations problems. Staff must still confirm the missed connection by comparing inbound gate arrival, transfer time and boarding cutoff, and seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed, and an offer isn't a booking until ticketed. Meals/hotel and any refund are judged separately (weather generally doesn't qualify for a standard hotel). I can't confirm any booking here.

cases.question: I got a text offering me another flight. Does that mean I'm booked?

matches.body:
## 2. Rebooking and passenger choice
Rebooking eligibility, an available offer and a confirmed ticket are different stages. Staff must explain which stage has actually been reached.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. Seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed.

### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

### 2.3 Passenger decision
Record an offer as OFFERED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED or EXPIRED, including its timestamp and notification channel. Expiry or silence does not prove acceptance. A passenger may decline an alternative without losing an otherwise qualifying refund option.

### 2.4 Boarding feasibility
An aircraft still at the gate may already be closed for boarding. Use recorded boarding events and realistic transfer constraints, rather than scheduled departure alone. Escalate conflicting timestamps instead of guessing.

### 2.5 Offer versus confirmed booking
A text offering another flight does not mean the passenger is booked. Distinguish SEARCHED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, TICKETED and FLOWN. Confirmation requires an actual ticketed reservation. If no seats are available, record NO_CURRENT_INVENTORY: recovery eligibility remains, but transport is not confirmed.

### 2.6 Changed routing
A different airport, additional connection or substantial arrival change may affect refund eligibility. Check accessibility needs before presenting a routing as suitable. Fare price alone does not establish suitability.

### 2.7 Required information
Record the original ticket, affected segments, boarding and arrival times, available alternatives, passenger choice and applicable policy version. An unresolved cause does not prevent protected rebooking; cause matters separately for passenger care.

### 2.8 Conflicting messages
A gate agent, app and phone agent may show different inventory snapshots. Identify the current offer and whether a ticket exists. Multiple messages are not multiple confirmed bookings. Tell the passenger which offer replaced an earlier proposal.

matches.body:
## 3. Qualifying disruption and passenger decision
The approved cause does not determine whether a cancellation or significant itinerary change qualifies. Weather-related changes can qualify just as airline-controlled changes can.

### 3.1 Cancellation
A canceled covered flight qualifies for assessment when the passenger declines substitute travel. Do not treat an ordinary delay as a cancellation. Verify the carrier's actual flight status.

### 3.2 Domestic significant-change threshold
A replacement scheduled to arrive at the final destination at least three hours later than originally scheduled meets the domestic arrival-change threshold. Departure at least three hours earlier can also qualify. Compare timezone-aware scheduled timestamps from the original ticket and replacement offer.

### 3.3 Passenger choice
Record whether the passenger requested a refund, declined replacement travel, accepted a credit or traveled. An unanswered offer does not prove acceptance or rejection. Verify delivery and expiry before deciding what response occurred.

### 3.4 Replacement flight already used
A passenger who flew the replacement generally cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under this disruption remedy. Arrival five hours late does not change that rule. Separate remedies for unused travel, downgrade or optional-service fees may still apply.

### 3.5 Final destination, not first-leg delay
A first flight arriving four hours late does not by itself establish the final-arrival change. A later connection may reduce the difference; a short inbound delay can also cause an overnight arrival change. Without replacement final-arrival information, the significant-change test remains unresolved.

### 3.6 Offer status
CREATED, DELIVERED, VIEWED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and FLOWN describe different events. DELIVERED means a notification reached the passenger's channel, not that they accepted travel. An internally generated voucher or offer does not close a refund request.

### 3.7 Partly used tickets
If the passenger flew the first segment but declines qualifying onward travel, assess the unused ticket portion using coupon accounting. Do not promise the entire fare or calculate a dollar amount without ticket-value records. Eligibility and refund amount are separate questions.

### 3.8 Other significant changes
A changed airport, additional connection or qualifying cabin downgrade may matter even when the arrival difference is under three hours. Compare the original and replacement itineraries before deciding. Duration is not the only qualifying criterion.

## 2. Cause codes
Each code describes the verified cause, not whether a hotel has been booked. Meal and hotel conditions still come from NS-CARE-2026.

### 2.1 Airline-controlled causes
MECHANICAL means an aircraft defect or maintenance hold under carrier responsibility. CREW_OPERATIONAL means an internal crew scheduling, reserve assignment or staffing problem. AIRLINE_OPERATIONS means carrier-controlled gate, baggage-loading, aircraft rotation or dispatch planning. Approved examples include a confirmed failed component or an internal reserve-assignment error.

### 2.2 Uncontrollable and unresolved causes
WEATHER means external weather conditions. ATC_EXTERNAL means an external air-traffic restriction. UNKNOWN means verified information is insufficient. MIXED_PENDING means multiple material causes exist and a controlling cause has not been assigned. Unresolved is not the same as uncontrollable.

matches.body:
## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization
Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher. Before booking independently, obtain written authorization stating the maximum reimbursable rate and approved dates. A receipt or verbal suggestion alone does not establish reimbursement approval.

### 4.7 Approved cause controls
The latest authorized, approved final investigation controls eligibility, even if a gate announcement initially said weather. A later unapproved draft cannot override an approved finding. Consult NS-CAUSE-2026 for investigation states.

### 4.8 Eligibility versus fulfillment
Full partner hotels do not remove eligibility. Record fulfillment separately as NOT_REQUESTED, SEARCHING, VOUCHER_AUTHORIZED, VOUCHER_ISSUED, RECEIPT_PENDING or CLOSED. Authorization is not proof of an issued voucher or booked room. Arrange alternative approved accommodation or escalate capacity problems.

### 4.9 Residence verification
Do not substitute billing address, nationality, telephone area code or trip origin for verified residence. Conflicting residence sources require authorized verification before deciding the home-metro condition.

## 3. Overnight hotels
A delayed arrival alone is insufficient for accommodation. Confirm the cause, overnight necessity and home-metro conditions together.

### 3.1 Standard hotel rule
Provide an approved hotel when a verified MECHANICAL or AIRLINE_OPERATIONS disruption makes an overnight stay necessary at the intermediate airport and the passenger is away from home. Authorized staff must issue the voucher or approve reimbursement in writing.

### 3.2 Crew-related exclusion
A final CREW_OPERATIONAL cause does not qualify for the standard overnight-hotel commitment in this edition. Crew scheduling problems, reserve shortages and rotation changes are excluded from this routine hotel benefit, even when attributable to Northstar. A duty manager may authorize discretionary assistance, but that is a courtesy rather than an entitlement.

### 3.3 Weather and unresolved causes
Weather and external air-traffic restrictions do not qualify for ordinary hotel assistance. Staff may provide local hotel information without promising airline payment. If the final cause is UNKNOWN or MIXED_PENDING, retain the case for review instead of assuming an exclusion.

### 3.4 Overnight and home-city restrictions
The passenger must need an overnight stay into the following calendar day because feasible onward travel is unavailable. A traveler stranded in their own home metropolitan area does not qualify for a standard room. Missing or conflicting residence information requires verification.

### 3.5 Courtesy exceptions
Crew-related hotel requests may be referred to a duty manager for an individually approved COURTESY booking. Record the approval and explain that this exception does not change the standard crew exclusion. Accessibility or safety needs require trained human review; a single courtesy booking does not establish general eligibility.

### 3.6 Date of service
Apply the edition in force when the disruption occurred, rather than the date on which an appeal or expense claim is reviewed. Retain the event date and applicable policy reference with the decision. Ask for the date when it is missing and materially affects the rule.

## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

### 3.1 Preliminary report
An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

matches.body:
## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization
Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher. Before booking independently, obtain written authorization stating the maximum reimbursable rate and approved dates. A receipt or verbal suggestion alone does not establish reimbursement approval.

### 4.7 Approved cause controls
The latest authorized, approved final investigation controls eligibility, even if a gate announcement initially said weather. A later unapproved draft cannot override an approved finding. Consult NS-CAUSE-2026 for investigation states.

### 4.8 Eligibility versus fulfillment
Full partner hotels do not remove eligibility. Record fulfillment separately as NOT_REQUESTED, SEARCHING, VOUCHER_AUTHORIZED, VOUCHER_ISSUED, RECEIPT_PENDING or CLOSED. Authorization is not proof of an issued voucher or booked room. Arrange alternative approved accommodation or escalate capacity problems.

### 4.9 Residence verification
Do not substitute billing address, nationality, telephone area code or trip origin for verified residence. Conflicting residence sources require authorized verification before deciding the home-metro condition.

## 3. Qualifying disruption and passenger decision
The approved cause does not determine whether a cancellation or significant itinerary change qualifies. Weather-related changes can qualify just as airline-controlled changes can.

### 3.1 Cancellation
A canceled covered flight qualifies for assessment when the passenger declines substitute travel. Do not treat an ordinary delay as a cancellation. Verify the carrier's actual flight status.

### 3.2 Domestic significant-change threshold
A replacement scheduled to arrive at the final destination at least three hours later than originally scheduled meets the domestic arrival-change threshold. Departure at least three hours earlier can also qualify. Compare timezone-aware scheduled timestamps from the original ticket and replacement offer.

### 3.3 Passenger choice
Record whether the passenger requested a refund, declined replacement travel, accepted a credit or traveled. An unanswered offer does not prove acceptance or rejection. Verify delivery and expiry before deciding what response occurred.

### 3.4 Replacement flight already used
A passenger who flew the replacement generally cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under this disruption remedy. Arrival five hours late does not change that rule. Separate remedies for unused travel, downgrade or optional-service fees may still apply.

### 3.5 Final destination, not first-leg delay
A first flight arriving four hours late does not by itself establish the final-arrival change. A later connection may reduce the difference; a short inbound delay can also cause an overnight arrival change. Without replacement final-arrival information, the significant-change test remains unresolved.

### 3.6 Offer status
CREATED, DELIVERED, VIEWED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and FLOWN describe different events. DELIVERED means a notification reached the passenger's channel, not that they accepted travel. An internally generated voucher or offer does not close a refund request.

### 3.7 Partly used tickets
If the passenger flew the first segment but declines qualifying onward travel, assess the unused ticket portion using coupon accounting. Do not promise the entire fare or calculate a dollar amount without ticket-value records. Eligibility and refund amount are separate questions.

### 3.8 Other significant changes
A changed airport, additional connection or qualifying cabin downgrade may matter even when the arrival difference is under three hours. Compare the original and replacement itineraries before deciding. Duration is not the only qualifying criterion.

answer.answer: Under the current policy (NS-CARE-2026, effective January 1, 2026), Northstar provides an approved hotel only when all four conditions hold together: (1) a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; (2) a final, approved airline-controlled cause — MECHANICAL, AIRLINE_OPERATIONS or CREW_OPERATIONAL (crew was added to coverage effective January 1, 2026); (3) onward travel genuinely requires waiting overnight at the affected airport, i.e. no feasible onward option can be completed without staying into the next calendar day; and (4) the passenger is away from their verified home metro area. An overnight delay by itself is not enough. Weather and external ATC disruptions are excluded, and UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or still-open investigations go to review rather than approval. Northstar normally issues a voucher; if you book your own room you need written authorization stating the maximum rate and dates first — a receipt alone is not approval. Eligibility is separate from an actually issued voucher or booked room.

cases.question: I'm stuck overnight because of bad weather. Will Northstar pay for my hotel?

matches.body:
## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization
Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher. Before booking independently, obtain written authorization stating the maximum reimbursable rate and approved dates. A receipt or verbal suggestion alone does not establish reimbursement approval.

### 4.7 Approved cause controls
The latest authorized, approved final investigation controls eligibility, even if a gate announcement initially said weather. A later unapproved draft cannot override an approved finding. Consult NS-CAUSE-2026 for investigation states.

### 4.8 Eligibility versus fulfillment
Full partner hotels do not remove eligibility. Record fulfillment separately as NOT_REQUESTED, SEARCHING, VOUCHER_AUTHORIZED, VOUCHER_ISSUED, RECEIPT_PENDING or CLOSED. Authorization is not proof of an issued voucher or booked room. Arrange alternative approved accommodation or escalate capacity problems.

### 4.9 Residence verification
Do not substitute billing address, nationality, telephone area code or trip origin for verified residence. Conflicting residence sources require authorized verification before deciding the home-metro condition.

## 3. Overnight hotels
A delayed arrival alone is insufficient for accommodation. Confirm the cause, overnight necessity and home-metro conditions together.

### 3.1 Standard hotel rule
Provide an approved hotel when a verified MECHANICAL or AIRLINE_OPERATIONS disruption makes an overnight stay necessary at the intermediate airport and the passenger is away from home. Authorized staff must issue the voucher or approve reimbursement in writing.

### 3.2 Crew-related exclusion
A final CREW_OPERATIONAL cause does not qualify for the standard overnight-hotel commitment in this edition. Crew scheduling problems, reserve shortages and rotation changes are excluded from this routine hotel benefit, even when attributable to Northstar. A duty manager may authorize discretionary assistance, but that is a courtesy rather than an entitlement.

### 3.3 Weather and unresolved causes
Weather and external air-traffic restrictions do not qualify for ordinary hotel assistance. Staff may provide local hotel information without promising airline payment. If the final cause is UNKNOWN or MIXED_PENDING, retain the case for review instead of assuming an exclusion.

### 3.4 Overnight and home-city restrictions
The passenger must need an overnight stay into the following calendar day because feasible onward travel is unavailable. A traveler stranded in their own home metropolitan area does not qualify for a standard room. Missing or conflicting residence information requires verification.

### 3.5 Courtesy exceptions
Crew-related hotel requests may be referred to a duty manager for an individually approved COURTESY booking. Record the approval and explain that this exception does not change the standard crew exclusion. Accessibility or safety needs require trained human review; a single courtesy booking does not establish general eligibility.

### 3.6 Date of service
Apply the edition in force when the disruption occurred, rather than the date on which an appeal or expense claim is reviewed. Retain the event date and applicable policy reference with the decision. Ask for the date when it is missing and materially affects the rule.

## 2. Rebooking and passenger choice
Rebooking eligibility, an available offer and a confirmed ticket are different stages. Staff must explain which stage has actually been reached.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. Seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed.

### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

### 2.3 Passenger decision
Record an offer as OFFERED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED or EXPIRED, including its timestamp and notification channel. Expiry or silence does not prove acceptance. A passenger may decline an alternative without losing an otherwise qualifying refund option.

### 2.4 Boarding feasibility
An aircraft still at the gate may already be closed for boarding. Use recorded boarding events and realistic transfer constraints, rather than scheduled departure alone. Escalate conflicting timestamps instead of guessing.

### 2.5 Offer versus confirmed booking
A text offering another flight does not mean the passenger is booked. Distinguish SEARCHED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, TICKETED and FLOWN. Confirmation requires an actual ticketed reservation. If no seats are available, record NO_CURRENT_INVENTORY: recovery eligibility remains, but transport is not confirmed.

### 2.6 Changed routing
A different airport, additional connection or substantial arrival change may affect refund eligibility. Check accessibility needs before presenting a routing as suitable. Fare price alone does not establish suitability.

### 2.7 Required information
Record the original ticket, affected segments, boarding and arrival times, available alternatives, passenger choice and applicable policy version. An unresolved cause does not prevent protected rebooking; cause matters separately for passenger care.

### 2.8 Conflicting messages
A gate agent, app and phone agent may show different inventory snapshots. Identify the current offer and whether a ticket exists. Multiple messages are not multiple confirmed bookings. Tell the passenger which offer replaced an earlier proposal.

matches.body:
## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

### 3.1 Preliminary report
An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

### 3.2 Cause not yet confirmed
UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an open investigation means NEEDS_REVIEW for hotel or meal decisions that depend on controllability. Request the approved cause rather than promising payment or treating uncertainty as a weather exclusion. Rebooking eligibility is assessed separately.

### 3.3 Final finding
An authorized analyst must identify the controlling cause, document the reasoning and sign the final revision. A finalized, approved mechanical finding can supersede an earlier provisional weather remark. Verify that the finding concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight.

### 3.4 Mixed causes
When weather and an internal problem both contributed, identify which cause prevented timely operation during the relevant interval. Do not count keywords or assume any weather mention excludes assistance. Keep MIXED_PENDING when the evidence cannot resolve the controlling cause.

### 3.5 Causal sequence
Weather may delay an aircraft before a later crew problem prevents departure. A maintenance note may concern a different aircraft after a swap. Compare the chronology and affected segment; the last event mentioned is not necessarily the controlling cause.

### 3.6 Evidence precedence
The latest authorized, signed final investigation takes precedence over preliminary gate comments. Preserve the earlier observation, its timestamp and the approved revision explaining the change. Operational timestamps establish when events occurred; they do not by themselves establish why. Never overwrite an earlier record to hide a changed decision.

### 3.7 Timestamp conflicts
Compare timezone-aware or UTC timestamps from reconciled operational records. A later ingestion time is not proof that an event happened later. If material times conflict, seek review rather than selecting the most convenient value.

### 3.8 Investigation states
The lifecycle is REPORTED, INVESTIGATING, PROPOSED and FINAL_APPROVED. PROPOSED is a draft awaiting authorized approval; it cannot override a valid approved finding. REOPENED means new evidence requires review of the earlier result. Keep the status and cause code as separate fields.

answer.answer: Under the current policy (NS-CARE-2026, effective January 1, 2026), a weather disruption does not qualify for Northstar's standard overnight hotel. Weather and external ATC causes are classed as uncontrollable and are excluded from standard hotel coverage, and an overnight delay by itself is never enough. The standard hotel requires all four conditions together: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary, a final approved airline-controlled cause (mechanical, airline operations, or — since 1 January 2026 — crew operational), a genuine overnight wait at the affected airport, and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. Important caveats: a gate announcement saying "weather" is not an approved finding; the latest authorized final investigation controls, and if the cause is UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or still under investigation, the case is held for review rather than refused. Separately, no-additional-fare rebooking under NS-CONN-2026 does apply to weather disruptions. Any self-booked hotel needs prior written authorization.

## 3. Overnight hotels
A delayed arrival alone is insufficient for accommodation. Confirm the cause, overnight necessity and home-metro conditions together.

### 3.1 Standard hotel rule
Provide an approved hotel when a verified MECHANICAL or AIRLINE_OPERATIONS disruption makes an overnight stay necessary at the intermediate airport and the passenger is away from home. Authorized staff must issue the voucher or approve reimbursement in writing.

### 3.2 Crew-related exclusion
A final CREW_OPERATIONAL cause does not qualify for the standard overnight-hotel commitment in this edition. Crew scheduling problems, reserve shortages and rotation changes are excluded from this routine hotel benefit, even when attributable to Northstar. A duty manager may authorize discretionary assistance, but that is a courtesy rather than an entitlement.

### 3.3 Weather and unresolved causes
Weather and external air-traffic restrictions do not qualify for ordinary hotel assistance. Staff may provide local hotel information without promising airline payment. If the final cause is UNKNOWN or MIXED_PENDING, retain the case for review instead of assuming an exclusion.

### 3.4 Overnight and home-city restrictions
The passenger must need an overnight stay into the following calendar day because feasible onward travel is unavailable. A traveler stranded in their own home metropolitan area does not qualify for a standard room. Missing or conflicting residence information requires verification.

### 3.5 Courtesy exceptions
Crew-related hotel requests may be referred to a duty manager for an individually approved COURTESY booking. Record the approval and explain that this exception does not change the standard crew exclusion. Accessibility or safety needs require trained human review; a single courtesy booking does not establish general eligibility.

### 3.6 Date of service
Apply the edition in force when the disruption occurred, rather than the date on which an appeal or expense claim is reviewed. Retain the event date and applicable policy reference with the decision. Ask for the date when it is missing and materially affects the rule.

## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization
Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher. Before booking independently, obtain written authorization stating the maximum reimbursable rate and approved dates. A receipt or verbal suggestion alone does not establish reimbursement approval.

### 4.7 Approved cause controls
The latest authorized, approved final investigation controls eligibility, even if a gate announcement initially said weather. A later unapproved draft cannot override an approved finding. Consult NS-CAUSE-2026 for investigation states.

### 4.8 Eligibility versus fulfillment
Full partner hotels do not remove eligibility. Record fulfillment separately as NOT_REQUESTED, SEARCHING, VOUCHER_AUTHORIZED, VOUCHER_ISSUED, RECEIPT_PENDING or CLOSED. Authorization is not proof of an issued voucher or booked room. Arrange alternative approved accommodation or escalate capacity problems.

### 4.9 Residence verification
Do not substitute billing address, nationality, telephone area code or trip origin for verified residence. Conflicting residence sources require authorized verification before deciding the home-metro condition.

## 2. Rebooking and passenger choice
Rebooking eligibility, an available offer and a confirmed ticket are different stages. Staff must explain which stage has actually been reached.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. Seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed.

### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

### 2.3 Passenger decision
Record an offer as OFFERED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED or EXPIRED, including its timestamp and notification channel. Expiry or silence does not prove acceptance. A passenger may decline an alternative without losing an otherwise qualifying refund option.

### 2.4 Boarding feasibility
An aircraft still at the gate may already be closed for boarding. Use recorded boarding events and realistic transfer constraints, rather than scheduled departure alone. Escalate conflicting timestamps instead of guessing.

### 2.5 Offer versus confirmed booking
A text offering another flight does not mean the passenger is booked. Distinguish SEARCHED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, TICKETED and FLOWN. Confirmation requires an actual ticketed reservation. If no seats are available, record NO_CURRENT_INVENTORY: recovery eligibility remains, but transport is not confirmed.

### 2.6 Changed routing

## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

### 3.1 Preliminary report
An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

### 3.2 Cause not yet confirmed
UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an open investigation means NEEDS_REVIEW for hotel or meal decisions that depend on controllability. Request the approved cause rather than promising payment or treating uncertainty as a weather exclusion. Rebooking eligibility is assessed separately.

### 3.3 Final finding
An authorized analyst must identify the controlling cause, document the reasoning and sign the final revision. A finalized, approved mechanical finding can supersede an earlier provisional weather remark. Verify that the finding concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight.

### 3.4 Mixed causes
When weather and an internal problem both contributed, identify which cause prevented timely operation during the relevant interval. Do not count keywords or assume any weather mention excludes assistance. Keep MIXED_PENDING when the evidence cannot resolve the controlling cause.

### 3.5 Causal sequence
Weather may delay an aircraft before a later crew problem prevents departure. A maintenance note may concern a different aircraft after a swap. Compare the chronology and affected segment; the last event mentioned is not necessarily the controlling cause.

### 3.6 Evidence precedence
The latest authorized, signed final investigation takes precedence over preliminary gate comments. Preserve the earlier observation, its timestamp and the approved revision explaining the change. Operational timestamps establish when events occurred; they do not by themselves establish why. Never overwrite an earlier record to hide a changed decision.

### 3.7 Timestamp conflicts
Compare timezone-aware or UTC timestamps from reconciled operational records. A later ingestion time is not proof that an event happened later. If material times conflict, seek review rather than selecting the most convenient value.

### 3.8 Investigation states
The lifecycle is REPORTED, INVESTIGATING, PROPOSED and FINAL_APPROVED. PROPOSED is a draft awaiting authorized approval; it cannot override a valid approved finding. REOPENED means new evidence requires review of the earlier result. Keep the status and cause code as separate fields.

answer.answer: Under the current policy (NS-CARE-2026, effective January 1, 2026), a crew scheduling problem can qualify for an overnight hotel. CREW_OPERATIONAL is an airline-controlled cause, and crew coverage was added to standard hotel eligibility from 1 January 2026 (the 2025 edition excluded it). Eligibility still requires all four conditions together: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final, approved airline-controlled cause; a genuine overnight wait at the recovery airport because no reasonable onward travel can be completed that day; and that you are away from your verified home metro area. A gate or dispatcher remark is only provisional — the approved final investigation finding controls, and an unresolved cause (UNKNOWN/MIXED_PENDING) goes to review. Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher; if you book your own room, get written authorization first stating the maximum rate and dates. Eligibility is separate from an actually issued voucher or booked room.

## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization
Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher. Before booking independently, obtain written authorization stating the maximum reimbursable rate and approved dates. A receipt or verbal suggestion alone does not establish reimbursement approval.

### 4.7 Approved cause controls
The latest authorized, approved final investigation controls eligibility, even if a gate announcement initially said weather. A later unapproved draft cannot override an approved finding. Consult NS-CAUSE-2026 for investigation states.

Full partner hotels do not remove eligibility. Record fulfillment separately as NOT_REQUESTED, SEARCHING, VOUCHER_AUTHORIZED, VOUCHER_ISSUED, RECEIPT_PENDING or CLOSED. ### 4.9 Residence verification
Do not substitute billing address, nationality, telephone area code or trip origin for verified residence. Conflicting residence sources require authorized verification before deciding the home-metro condition.

## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

### 3.1 Preliminary report
An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

### 3.2 Cause not yet confirmed
UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an open investigation means NEEDS_REVIEW for hotel or meal decisions that depend on controllability. Request the approved cause rather than promising payment or treating uncertainty as a weather exclusion. Rebooking eligibility is assessed separately.

### 3.3 Final finding
An authorized analyst must identify the controlling cause, document the reasoning and sign the final revision. A finalized, approved mechanical finding can supersede an earlier provisional weather remark. Verify that the finding concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight.

### 3.4 Mixed causes
When weather and an internal problem both contributed, identify which cause prevented timely operation during the relevant interval. Do not count keywords or assume any weather mention excludes assistance. Keep MIXED_PENDING when the evidence cannot resolve the controlling cause.

### 3.5 Causal sequence
Weather may delay an aircraft before a later crew problem prevents departure. A maintenance note may concern a different aircraft after a swap. Compare the chronology and affected segment; the last event mentioned is not necessarily the controlling cause.

### 3.6 Evidence precedence
The latest authorized, signed final investigation takes precedence over preliminary gate comments. Preserve the earlier observation, its timestamp and the approved revision explaining the change. Operational timestamps establish when events occurred; they do not by themselves establish why. Never overwrite an earlier record to hide a changed decision.

### 3.7 Timestamp conflicts
Compare timezone-aware or UTC timestamps from reconciled operational records. A later ingestion time is not proof that an event happened later. If material times conflict, seek review rather than selecting the most convenient value.

### 3.8 Investigation states
The lifecycle is REPORTED, INVESTIGATING, PROPOSED and FINAL_APPROVED. PROPOSED is a draft awaiting authorized approval; it cannot override a valid approved finding. REOPENED means new evidence requires review of the earlier result. Keep the status and cause code as separate fields.

answer.answer: Yes — in principle. Under the current refund policy (NS-REF-2026 v2.0, effective 1 January 2026), a replacement flight scheduled to arrive at your **final destination** at least three hours later than your original ticket meets the domestic significant-change threshold. If you decline that changed itinerary and don't accept replacement travel, a credit or other compensation, the disruption can qualify for a refund; rejecting an eligible rebooking does not forfeit it. The cause doesn't matter — weather-related changes qualify the same as airline-controlled ones. Two cautions: the three hours is measured by comparing timezone-aware scheduled arrival times at the final destination (a three-hour first-leg delay alone doesn't count), and if you actually fly the replacement you generally can't get a refund for transportation used. A wholly unused qualifying ticket may be refunded in full; partly used tickets are calculated from coupon accounting, returned to the original payment method (targets: 7 business days by card, 20 calendar days otherwise).

cases.question: I took the replacement flight, but I arrived five hours late. Can I still get a full refund?

matches.body:
## 3. Qualifying disruption and passenger decision
The approved cause does not determine whether a cancellation or significant itinerary change qualifies. Weather-related changes can qualify just as airline-controlled changes can.

### 3.1 Cancellation
A canceled covered flight qualifies for assessment when the passenger declines substitute travel. Do not treat an ordinary delay as a cancellation. Verify the carrier's actual flight status.

### 3.2 Domestic significant-change threshold
A replacement scheduled to arrive at the final destination at least three hours later than originally scheduled meets the domestic arrival-change threshold. Departure at least three hours earlier can also qualify. Compare timezone-aware scheduled timestamps from the original ticket and replacement offer.

### 3.3 Passenger choice
Record whether the passenger requested a refund, declined replacement travel, accepted a credit or traveled. An unanswered offer does not prove acceptance or rejection. Verify delivery and expiry before deciding what response occurred.

### 3.4 Replacement flight already used
A passenger who flew the replacement generally cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under this disruption remedy. Arrival five hours late does not change that rule. Separate remedies for unused travel, downgrade or optional-service fees may still apply.

### 3.5 Final destination, not first-leg delay
A first flight arriving four hours late does not by itself establish the final-arrival change. A later connection may reduce the difference; a short inbound delay can also cause an overnight arrival change. Without replacement final-arrival information, the significant-change test remains unresolved.

### 3.6 Offer status
CREATED, DELIVERED, VIEWED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and FLOWN describe different events. DELIVERED means a notification reached the passenger's channel, not that they accepted travel. An internally generated voucher or offer does not close a refund request.

### 3.7 Partly used tickets
If the passenger flew the first segment but declines qualifying onward travel, assess the unused ticket portion using coupon accounting. Do not promise the entire fare or calculate a dollar amount without ticket-value records. Eligibility and refund amount are separate questions.

### 3.8 Other significant changes
A changed airport, additional connection or qualifying cabin downgrade may matter even when the arrival difference is under three hours. Compare the original and replacement itineraries before deciding. Duration is not the only qualifying criterion.

## 2. Rebooking and passenger choice
Rebooking eligibility, an available offer and a confirmed ticket are different stages. Staff must explain which stage has actually been reached.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. Seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed.

### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

### 2.3 Passenger decision
Record an offer as OFFERED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED or EXPIRED, including its timestamp and notification channel. Expiry or silence does not prove acceptance. A passenger may decline an alternative without losing an otherwise qualifying refund option.

### 2.4 Boarding feasibility
An aircraft still at the gate may already be closed for boarding. Use recorded boarding events and realistic transfer constraints, rather than scheduled departure alone. Escalate conflicting timestamps instead of guessing.

### 2.5 Offer versus confirmed booking
A text offering another flight does not mean the passenger is booked. Distinguish SEARCHED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, TICKETED and FLOWN. Confirmation requires an actual ticketed reservation. If no seats are available, record NO_CURRENT_INVENTORY: recovery eligibility remains, but transport is not confirmed.

A different airport, additional connection or substantial arrival change may affect refund eligibility. Check accessibility needs before presenting a routing as suitable. Fare price alone does not establish suitability.

### 2.7 Required information

### 2.8 Conflicting messages

## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization
Northstar normally issues an approved hotel voucher. Before booking independently, obtain written authorization stating the maximum reimbursable rate and approved dates. A receipt or verbal suggestion alone does not establish reimbursement approval.

### 4.7 Approved cause controls
The latest authorized, approved final investigation controls eligibility, even if a gate announcement initially said weather. A later unapproved draft cannot override an approved finding. Consult NS-CAUSE-2026 for investigation states.

### 4.8 Eligibility versus fulfillment
Full partner hotels do not remove eligibility. Record fulfillment separately as NOT_REQUESTED, SEARCHING, VOUCHER_AUTHORIZED, VOUCHER_ISSUED, RECEIPT_PENDING or CLOSED. Authorization is not proof of an issued voucher or booked room. Arrange alternative approved accommodation or escalate capacity problems.

### 4.9 Residence verification
Do not substitute billing address, nationality, telephone area code or trip origin for verified residence. Conflicting residence sources require authorized verification before deciding the home-metro condition.

## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

### 3.1 Preliminary report
An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

### 3.2 Cause not yet confirmed
UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an open investigation means NEEDS_REVIEW for hotel or meal decisions that depend on controllability. Request the approved cause rather than promising payment or treating uncertainty as a weather exclusion. Rebooking eligibility is assessed separately.

### 3.3 Final finding
An authorized analyst must identify the controlling cause, document the reasoning and sign the final revision. A finalized, approved mechanical finding can supersede an earlier provisional weather remark. Verify that the finding concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight.

### 3.4 Mixed causes
When weather and an internal problem both contributed, identify which cause prevented timely operation during the relevant interval. Do not count keywords or assume any weather mention excludes assistance. Keep MIXED_PENDING when the evidence cannot resolve the controlling cause.

### 3.5 Causal sequence
Weather may delay an aircraft before a later crew problem prevents departure. A maintenance note may concern a different aircraft after a swap. Compare the chronology and affected segment; the last event mentioned is not necessarily the controlling cause.

### 3.6 Evidence precedence
The latest authorized, signed final investigation takes precedence over preliminary gate comments. Preserve the earlier observation, its timestamp and the approved revision explaining the change. Operational timestamps establish when events occurred; they do not by themselves establish why. Never overwrite an earlier record to hide a changed decision.

### 3.7 Timestamp conflicts
Compare timezone-aware or UTC timestamps from reconciled operational records. A later ingestion time is not proof that an event happened later. If material times conflict, seek review rather than selecting the most convenient value.

### 3.8 Investigation states
The lifecycle is REPORTED, INVESTIGATING, PROPOSED and FINAL_APPROVED. PROPOSED is a draft awaiting authorized approval; it cannot override a valid approved finding. REOPENED means new evidence requires review of the earlier result. Keep the status and cause code as separate fields.

answer.answer: Generally no. Under the current refund policy (NS-REF-2026, effective 1 January 2026), a passenger who actually flew the replacement flight cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under the disruption remedy, and arriving five hours late does not change that rule — the three-hour significant-change threshold matters when you decline the replacement, not after you have travelled on it. Other remedies can still exist: refunds for any unused portion of the ticket (assessed by coupon accounting), a qualifying cabin downgrade, or optional-service fees for services not provided. A full refund is normally available only for an entirely unused qualifying ticket; partly used tickets are calculated from accounting records rather than estimated from the length of the delay. Eligible refunds go back to the original form of payment, with processing targets of seven business days (credit card) or twenty calendar days (other methods).

## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. ### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

## 2. Rebooking and passenger choice
Rebooking eligibility, an available offer and a confirmed ticket are different stages. Staff must explain which stage has actually been reached.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. Seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed.

### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

### 2.3 Passenger decision
Record an offer as OFFERED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED or EXPIRED, including its timestamp and notification channel. Expiry or silence does not prove acceptance. A passenger may decline an alternative without losing an otherwise qualifying refund option.

### 2.4 Boarding feasibility
An aircraft still at the gate may already be closed for boarding. Use recorded boarding events and realistic transfer constraints, rather than scheduled departure alone. Escalate conflicting timestamps instead of guessing.

### 2.5 Offer versus confirmed booking

A delayed arrival alone is insufficient for accommodation. Confirm the cause, overnight necessity and home-metro conditions together.

answer.answer: Under the current rules (NS-CAUSE-2026, effective 1 Jan 2026), the final approved investigation controls. A gate or dispatcher report is only PROVISIONAL "" it can explain why an investigation was opened but cannot by itself grant or deny cause-dependent assistance. Once an authorized analyst documents and signs a FINAL_APPROVED finding, that mechanical classification supersedes the earlier weather remark, provided it concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight. The earlier weather observation and its timestamp are preserved, not deleted, with the approved revision explaining the change; a merely PROPOSED draft could not override an approved finding. MECHANICAL is an airline-controlled cause, so it can satisfy the controllability requirement for meal vouchers (after three hours' wait) and for a standard hotel "" but the overnight-necessity, away-from-home-metro and valid-itinerary conditions must also be met. Protected rebooking is assessed separately and does not depend on cause.

## 3. Qualifying disruption and passenger decision
The approved cause does not determine whether a cancellation or significant itinerary change qualifies. Weather-related changes can qualify just as airline-controlled changes can.

### 3.1 Cancellation
A canceled covered flight qualifies for assessment when the passenger declines substitute travel. Do not treat an ordinary delay as a cancellation. Verify the carrier's actual flight status.

### 3.2 Domestic significant-change threshold
A replacement scheduled to arrive at the final destination at least three hours later than originally scheduled meets the domestic arrival-change threshold. Departure at least three hours earlier can also qualify. Compare timezone-aware scheduled timestamps from the original ticket and replacement offer.

### 3.3 Passenger choice
Record whether the passenger requested a refund, declined replacement travel, accepted a credit or traveled. An unanswered offer does not prove acceptance or rejection. Verify delivery and expiry before deciding what response occurred.

### 3.4 Replacement flight already used
A passenger who flew the replacement generally cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under this disruption remedy. Arrival five hours late does not change that rule. Separate remedies for unused travel, downgrade or optional-service fees may still apply.

### 3.5 Final destination, not first-leg delay
A first flight arriving four hours late does not by itself establish the final-arrival change. A later connection may reduce the difference; a short inbound delay can also cause an overnight arrival change. Without replacement final-arrival information, the significant-change test remains unresolved.

### 3.6 Offer status
CREATED, DELIVERED, VIEWED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and FLOWN describe different events. DELIVERED means a notification reached the passenger's channel, not that they accepted travel. An internally generated voucher or offer does not close a refund request.

### 3.7 Partly used tickets
If the passenger flew the first segment but declines qualifying onward travel, assess the unused ticket portion using coupon accounting. Do not promise the entire fare or calculate a dollar amount without ticket-value records. Eligibility and refund amount are separate questions.

### 3.8 Other significant changes
A changed airport, additional connection or qualifying cabin downgrade may matter even when the arrival difference is under three hours. Compare the original and replacement itineraries before deciding. Duration is not the only qualifying criterion.

### 3.4 Replacement flight already used
A passenger who flew the replacement generally cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under this disruption remedy. Arrival five hours late does not change that rule. Separate remedies for unused travel, downgrade or optional-service fees may still apply.

### 3.5 Final destination, not first-leg delay
A first flight arriving four hours late does not by itself establish the final-arrival change. A later connection may reduce the difference; a short inbound delay can also cause an overnight arrival change. Without replacement final-arrival information, the significant-change test remains unresolved.

### 3.6 Offer status
CREATED, DELIVERED, VIEWED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and FLOWN describe different events. DELIVERED means a notification reached the passenger's channel, not that they accepted travel. An internally generated voucher or offer does not close a refund request.

### 3.7 Partly used tickets
If the passenger flew the first segment but declines qualifying onward travel, assess the unused ticket portion using coupon accounting. Do not promise the entire fare or calculate a dollar amount without ticket-value records. Eligibility and refund amount are separate questions.

### 3.8 Other significant changes
A changed airport, additional connection or qualifying cabin downgrade may matter even when the arrival difference is under three hours. Compare the original and replacement itineraries before deciding. Duration is not the only qualifying criterion.

For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. ### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved airline-controlled cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is included in current hotel coverage. A crew shortage or rotation problem can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 also hold. This inclusion took effect January 1, 2026.
